name: Hoover
why: A thick, badly out-of-tune saw stack across three octaves that swoops up into every note. It sounds like a vacuum cleaner, which is where the name comes from.

ingredients.name: Stack and detune hard
ingredients.adds: Five saws per note, much further apart than a trance lead.
ingredients.listenFor: It gets wide and a little sour. That sourness is the sound.

ingredients.name: Three octaves
ingredients.adds: Every note also plays an octave below and an octave above.
ingredients.listenFor: It fills the whole range at once.

ingredients.name: Swoop up
ingredients.adds: Each note starts low and slides up to pitch.
ingredients.listenFor: The "whooo" at the start of each note.

knobs.label: swoop
knobs.above: No swoop: just a detuned chord.

knobs.label: swoop time
knobs.below: Too fast to hear as a slide.

ingredients.name: Room
ingredients.adds: The warehouse it is played in.

pitfalls: Played as chords it turns to mud: the three octaves already are a chord.
